what_happened: Job 20261030-170805-jz9t ("Check reading's relied-on earlier-job files exist in the snapshot") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic found the plan well grounded: every function it names exists and the demonstrations use real seams. It left one major finding: the 8-word "new" exemption window covers every name after "adds" or "new". That contradicts the plan's own criterion 2 case ("adds X beside Y" must refuse an absent Y). It also switches off the symbol check for the usual reliance phrasing ("adds X, reusing Y"). There were two minor findings (Part 1 refuses any prose path missing from the snapshot, which goes beyond reliance on unlanded files; string literals and test fixtures count as existing code) and one nit (a garbled fixture path in the criterion 5 test). No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no repo checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planner designs the matching rule (the "new" exemption window, the corpus of existing code, the path scope) from the reading's wording. It never runs the rule against real reading phrasings, and it does not run the plan's own demonstration cases against the rule's design. The rule contradicted its own criterion 2 test, and an internal consistency check would have caught that. Athena's replay runs only on built code, so a plan-time flaw in a matching heuristic is found only when the critic traces it by hand. Planning has a fixed three rounds and keeps no partial plan. One late major therefore fails the job and loses the planning spend. This is the second job in a row in this area (reading checks) that has failed the same way. The rule's scope is also left loose (all prose paths, string literals as code), so each round exposes new over-match findings.
prevention: Add a plan-time step for any plan that adds or changes a matching, parsing or refusal rule. The planner must list the rule's exemption and match windows as concrete input and output cases, taken from real past reading phrasings. Athena would then run a small mechanical self-consistency pass over those cases. Each criterion's demonstration case must be reproducible by the rule as specified (for example, "adds X beside Y" must refuse an absent Y). The pass runs on every draft, and its result is fed back to the planner before the critic is called. The rule's scope must also be pinned to the reading's subject (names relied on from earlier unlanded jobs), not to all prose.
proposed_request: Add a check that refuses a reading which relies on files or symbols from an earlier job that are missing from the current snapshot. Scope: only names the reading says it relies on or reuses from an earlier job's output (for example "reusing Y", "beside Y", "from job <id>"). Do not check historical mentions, paths inside refused examples, or names the reading itself introduces. A name introduced by "adds" or "new" is exempt only for the name that marker introduces; any other name in the same clause (for example "adds X, reusing Y" or "adds X beside Y") must still be checked and refused if absent. Treat only non-comment, non-string-literal code lines in the snapshot as existing code. Chain the check after check_reading_acceptance inside read_once so the reader keeps its single correction. Acceptance: (1) a reading that relies on a symbol or file absent from the snapshot is refused with a message naming it; (2) "adds X beside Y" and "adds X, reusing Y" refuse an absent Y and pass an absent X; (3) names present in the snapshot pass; (4) names that appear only in string literals or test fixtures do not count as existing; (5) historical mentions and example paths in prose are not checked; (6) the reading for this job itself passes the new check. Each criterion gets exactly one demonstration that calls the production functions through real seams, and the fixture paths must be valid.
